text:
maria: quick sync — i'm prototyping a control-plane refactor for dedicated GPU pool autoscaling. pushed a strawman proto here: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/1234. main question: where to draw the interface boundary between control plane and operator?

ravi: tl;dr: do we want the operator to make admission decisions (prewarm/node lifecycle) or should control plane own admission and just call operator for node operations?

sara: my vote: keep operator thin. operator = dumb node manager (create/destroy, drain), control plane = brains (admit, prewarm tokens, billing signals). avoids duplicate policy.

mike: +1 for separation but speed matters. if control plane blocks on operator API for every admit, latency spikes. can we do async admits with short-lived tokens?

maria: idea in proto: control plane returns an admit token (ttl 30s) and operator trusts token to attach prewarm credits locally. operator reconciles node state eventually. this lets fast admits.

lee: concern: token replay + security. need signed token, short ttl, and operator verifies signature via KMS or control plane pubkey. also need metrics for admit -> node up timeline.

maria: agreed. sketch in PR includes JWT-ish token signed by control plane key and fields: tenant, admit_id, ttl, prewarm_amount.

ravi: what about fallbacks when operator-side provisioning fails? fallback to a smaller model variant served on hot path?

sara: we have existing fallback logic in runtime. proposal: control plane chooses fallback policy based on SLA tier and cost band. operator reports failure cause back to control plane via events so decision can be updated.

mike: telemetry: add counters for admit_token_issued, operator_ack, node_ready_ms, fallback_triggered. that will let us tune token ttl and retry window.

lee: rollout plan? prefer canary by tenant / dedicated pools. also a kill-switch via feature flag in control plane and operator version check.

maria: yep. propose phased rollout: 1) internal prod canary (10 tenants), 2) opt-in customers, 3) default. PR has feature flag gates and a compatibility shim for older operators.

infra-bot: deploybot: canary cluster deploy started for branch control-plane-refactor at 1749999995 — https://deploys.redwood/aws/4567

ravi: one more tradeoff: where to store admission history? control plane DB or operator local cache? we need global visibility for accounting. store authoritative state in control plane, operator keeps local cache for speed.

sara: action items: maria to update proto with signed token format + metrics hooks; mike to add telemetry counters; lee to draft canary playbook; ravi to add operator shim design. we aim for RFC follow-up meeting next wed.

maria: thanks — i'll update PR and ping async. :thumbsup:
